data.title: NEC exhibits at the 32nd ITS World Congress, a conference and exhibition focused on mobility
data.description:
TOKYO, Oct 16, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - NEC Corporation (NEC; TSE: 6701) has announced its participation in the upcoming 32nd ITS World Congress as an exhibitor at the ITS Japan Pavilion, which will showcase public- and private-sector exhibitors affiliated with ITS Japan. Additionally, NEC will present a technical paper during a session at the event. This five-day conference and exhibition, which brings together experts from industry, government, and academia, focuses on intelligent transport systems (ITS) and will be held in Gangneung, Korea, from October 19 (Monday) to October 23 (Friday), 2026 (ITS Japan Pavilion; Booth number: S25).

The ITS World Congress, which aims to solve road traffic problems through the widespread adoption of ITS and to create business opportunities, is the only world congress co-organized annually by three key ITS organizations from around the globe (Europe: ERTICO; the Americas: ITS America; the Asia-Pacific region: ITS Asia-Pacific). This event features a vast variety of technical sessions, exhibits, panel discussions and more, serving as a forum for participants to exchange information from diverse perspectives on a wide range of topics, including technological development and market trends.

Exhibit Overview

Based on the concept of "Shaping the Mobility of Tomorrow," NEC aims to harness ICT and utilize road infrastructure and related data to create new environmentally friendly mobility services that ensure safety, security, and convenience. Moreover, the data collected through these services will be integrated and used to facilitate smarter, more sustainable and efficient transportation.

At this year's ITS World Congress, NEC will use domestic and global case studies, videos, and panels to introduce a solution that combines three core technologies to achieve next-generation traffic control integrated with physical AI on expressways: (1) digital twin data-fusion technology, (2) wrong-way driving detection utilizing fiber-optic sensing, and (3) individual vehicle monitoring technology using long-range LiDAR for driving safety support.

These technologies will advance the evolution of social infrastructure, including distributed edge AI processing platforms, by enabling spatiotemporal synchronization of sensor data collected across wide areas using fiber-optic sensing.

(1) Road State Monitoring with Multimodal Sensing

On a digital twin platform with real-time spatiotemporal synchronization, data fusion technology enables both real-time, detailed monitoring of road environments and the intelligent transformation of regional road networks.

(2) Wrong-way Driving Detection Using Distributed Fiber-Optic Sensing

By utilizing continuous sensing along an entire route, monitoring blind spots can be eliminated. This allows for the collection of early warning information, enabling early detection of unforeseen circumstances, such as vehicles traveling in the wrong direction or obstacles on the road. In addition, traffic flow and safety are improved by alerting following vehicles to take evasive action.

(3) LiDAR Sensing Technology for Driving Safety Support on Expressways

Capable of capturing 3D expressway information in real time, LiDAR technology is used to detect and track moving vehicles while quickly providing traffic condition updates to autonomous and other vehicles, thus promoting safe driving. The results of field trials conducted on expressways will also be presented during the poster presentation and at the booth exhibit featuring the accepted technical paper.

Going forward, NEC will leverage its ICT infrastructure technology and proprietary analytical AI to deliver digital infrastructure for the AI Transformation (AX*) era. This infrastructure will enable the deployment of physical AI across regional road networks through digital twins that are spatiotemporally synchronized in real time.

(*) AI Transformation (AX) refers to initiatives that go beyond simply implementing AI as a tool. Instead, AX involves reshaping business processes, business models, and organizational culture based on AI.

About NEC

The NEC Group leverages technology to create social value and promote a more sustainable world where everyone has the chance to reach their full potential. NEC Corporation was established in 1899. Today, the NEC Group's approximately 110,000 employees utilize world-leading AI, security, and communications technologies to solve the most pressing needs of customers and society.

For more information, please visit https://www.nec.com, and follow us on LinkedIn and YouTube.

Source: NEC Corporation

data.title: HDFC, ICICI Bank Q2 earnings preview: deposit surge, margin pressure in focus
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 16 -- HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, India's two largest private sector banks, are likely to face a similar challenge in the September quarter - sustaining loan growth without sacrificing margins as deposit costs rise, according to three brokerages

When the two lenders report their Q2 earnings on Saturday, investors will closely track their net interest margins (NIMs), credit costs and management commentary on growth. Robust deposit mobilisation led by robust foreign currency non-resident bank or FCNR(B) deposits and resilient asset quality are expected to support the performance of the banks.

For HDFC Bank, the focus will be on the execution by the new management, the impact of FCNR(B) deposits, and translating improved operating efficiency into stronger profitability.

ICICI Bank, meanwhile, is expected to report healthy business growth, although a surge in FCNR(B) deposits could weigh on margins in the near term.

According to Bloomberg's estimates, HDFC Bank is expected to post a net profit of Rs.21,108 crore, up 13% on year and 10% on quarter. This is likely to be driven by strong loan growth, supported by corporate and small and medium enterprise lending, and by deposit growth.

Provisional data shared with the exchanges showed that HDFC Bank's gross advances grew 16.3% year-on-year in the September quarter, while deposits rose 18.8%. The bank mobilized $11.5 billion in FCNR(B) deposits, against which its overseas branches extended $5.7 billion in loans. However, its current account and savings account (CASA) ratio fell around 70 basis points sequentially to 31.6%, highlighting pressure on its low-cost deposit mix.

"The headline reported numbers on loan growth is marginally lower than industry average. Credit to deposit (CD) ratio was stable on a period-ending basis at 95% led as impact of FCNR deposits has been lower. Deposits grew 19% on year. We are building NIM (net interest margins) to remain stable or marginally decline this quarter," Kotak Institutional Equities said in a report on HDFC Bank.

For the quarter ended June, the bank's NIM was 3.26%, lower than 3.4% a quarter ago. Motilal Oswal Financial Services expects margins to moderate by eight basis points in the September quarter. Yes Securities also expects sequential margin pressure as deposit costs rise faster than yields on advances.

Analysts expect asset quality to remain contained at around 45-50 bps. "We expect the gross NPL (non-performing loan ratio) to be stable with slippages at 1.2% of loans. Near-term focus would be the progress of NIM (NIM to improve slower-than-expected), impact of FCNR deposits and execution under the new management," Kotak said.

Earlier this month, RBI approved the appointment of Anup Bagchi as the new managing director and chief executive officer of HDFC Bank for a three-year term starting 27 October, succeeding Sashidhar Jagdishan, whose term ends on 26 October.

"The appointment of Mr. Bagchi removes a key overhang surrounding HDFC Bank's leadership succession and brings an external perspective at a time when the bank is seeking to rebuild investor confidence," Motilal Oswal had said in a report, adding that a new leadership team, alongside an improvement in growth and earnings trajectory, should improve investor sentiment.

ICICI Bank is expected to deliver stronger headline loan growth, aided by FCNR(B) inflows, even as the resulting funding mix puts pressure on margins.

Motilal Oswal has pegged the bank's loan growth at 26% year-on-year and 9% quarter-on-quarter, while deposits are expected to rise over 25% on year and 10% sequentially. The brokerage expects the bank's net profit to rise 19% on year to Rs.14,648 crore. In the previous quarter, its bottomline was at Rs.14,805 crore.

Kotak Institutional Equities expects around 15% on year growth in pre-provision operating profit, supported by healthy revenue growth. However, it expects the bank's NIMs to decline by 15 bps sequentially to 3.8%, primarily because of FCNR(B) deposits raised during the quarter.

For the quarter ended June, the bank's NIM was at 4.36% against 4.32% a quarter ago.

Motilal Oswal also expects a 20-bps sequential fall in NIMs, citing the higher leverage component of FCNR(B) inflows.

Asset quality is expected to remain resilient. Kotak estimates credit costs at around 0.4%, with slippages at approximately 1.5% of loans, and does not anticipate fresh negative surprises on provisions. Motilal Oswal expects a marginal sequential increase in provisioning due to higher standard asset requirements on the leveraged portion of FCNR(B) inflows.

data.title: Pulse of the Street: Best week since April puts recovery to the earnings test
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 16 -- Indian stocks have staged their strongest weekly rally since April, but the rebound has yet to broaden beyond the largest companies. A sharp rally in information technology (IT) stocks, and a firmer rupee lifted benchmarks, while foreign investors continued to sell and crude oil above $100 a barrel kept pressure on corporate earnings.

The Sensex gained 3.13% and the Nifty 50 rose 2.79% in the week ended 16 October, their biggest weekly advances since the week ended 10 April. On Friday, the Sensex climbed 0.56% to 74,729.27, while the Nifty advanced 0.65% to 23,146.15.

The gains extended the previous week's rebound, which broke an eight-week losing streak. The challenge now is to turn that recovery into a broader advance backed by earnings rather than sentiment alone.

The Indian rupee strengthened to Rs.94.96 against the dollar on Friday from Rs.96.74 a week earlier, easing currency pressures.

Sanjit Singh Paul, smallcase manager and managing director at Modulor Capital, attributed the rebound to Reserve Bank of India (RBI) measures supporting the rupee, softer US yields, positive IT results and domestic institutional buying. The RBI opened a special dollar window for oil companies, diverting their demand from the spot market, and tightened currency-hedging rules.

But the stock-market rally has yet to spread across the broader market. The BSE LargeCap index gained 1.85% during the week, outpacing the MidCap index's 0.99% rise, while the SmallCap index slipped 0.02%.

Paul cautioned that midcap, smallcap and microcap stocks had not kept pace with the benchmark rally. "The current move is definitely worth watching, but has not established itself as sustainable," he said.

Domestic institutional investors net bought Rs.11,474 crore of Indian equities during the week through Thursday, cushioning continued foreign selling. Foreign portfolio investors net sold Rs.538 crore over the same period.

Prashant Singhal, partner and leader, Clients & Industries, EY India, pointed to systematic investment plan contributions as a source of domestic support. Resilient consumption, industrial activity and manufacturing also supported his positive longer-term outlook.

The BSE Information Technology index surged 11%, bucking sharp losses in Asian technology markets. The rally followed a sell-off that had left valuations more attractive and expectations for earnings more favourable.

Gurmeet Singh Chawla, managing director at Master Portfolio Services Ltd, attributed the rebound to cheaper valuations, better earnings expectations and short covering. "Sentiment alone won't hold the rally, though. Companies will need to show faster revenue growth and a healthy deal pipeline," Chawla said.

Paul said contract wins, better margins and AI-generated revenue supported Indian IT results. Overseas semiconductor stocks, by contrast, faced concerns about valuations, financing costs and returns on infrastructure spending. "The gains do have a credible earnings foundation."

Yet improving results at larger companies do not necessarily signal a broader revival in technology spending. Sustaining the rally would require stronger organic revenue growth, Paul added. A firmer rupee could also erode the currency benefit that supported margins in the latest quarter, while delayed client spending remained a risk.

Beyond IT, the BSE Auto index gained 3.4% and Realty rose 2.8%. Utilities and Oil & Gas advanced 2.1% each, while Metal climbed 1.8%. Healthcare fell 1.1%, Services slipped 0.9% and FMCG declined 0.3%.

Global markets offered a mixed backdrop. US consumer prices rose 3.7% year-on-year in September, pushing expectations of an October Federal Reserve rate increase to roughly 50% after Wednesday's release. Concerns about financing AI infrastructure also weighed on technology stocks.

Asian markets were particularly weak. Indonesia's Jakarta Composite and South Korea's Kospi fell about 15% each, while Taiwan's Taiex lost 4.5% and Japan's Nikkei 225 declined 5.3%. In Europe, Britain's FTSE 100 and France's CAC 40 gained 2.77% and 2.15%, respectively. The Nifty ranked among the best-performing global benchmarks tracked during the week.

Crude oil remained a key risk for Indian companies despite a modest easing in prices. Brent crude spot price slipped 0.36% during the week to $104.43 a barrel. US 10-year Treasury yields declined to about 5.09% on Friday from 5.21% on 13 October.

Paul cautioned that oil above $100 continued to threaten corporate margins. Passing higher costs on to customers could weaken demand, adding another constraint on earnings growth.

Investors will also look to banks for evidence that the recovery can extend beyond IT. The Union cabinet on Wednesday approved the sale of a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to a Fairfax Financial Holdings entity for about Rs.52,877 crore. The transaction comprises the government's 30.48% holding and LIC's 30.24% stake.

Attention now turns to bank earnings and management commentary, particularly from HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, alongside the domestic interest-rate outlook, Paul said.

"The rally can run longer if earnings stay strong, crude eases and foreign selling slows. If not, the current strength may turn out to be only a short-term rebound," Chawla said.

Next week has four trading sessions, with markets closed on Tuesday for Dussehra. The more immediate test, however, is whether the rally can draw in more stocks beyond the headline indices. "More stocks need to join the headline index-led rally to determine whether gains continue or fizzle out," Paul said.

data.title: Southwest Airlines Q3 setup: Guidance faces earnings-revision test
data.description:
Southwest Airlines is set to report third-quarter 2026 results on October 21 after the market closes. Wall Street expects non-GAAP EPS of $0.57 and revenue of $8.24B, but earnings expectations have weakened, with 16 downward EPS revisions versus two upward revisions over the past three months.

The shares traded near $41.15 on Friday, leaving the stock down 0.80% year to date, compared with a 13.13% gain for the S&P 500 (SP500).

Revenue growth and fuel costs are the key factors to watch, with adjusted unit revenue rising 20.1% YoY. For the third quarter, management expects adjusted unit revenue growth of 17.5%–19.5%, supported by its commercial overhaul, including bag fees and assigned seating.

Fuel remains a major risk. The second-quarter fuel costs rose to $3.92 per gallon from $2.32 a year earlier, adding $889M in expenses and creating a $1.17-per-share adjusted earnings headwind.

Management expects third-quarter fuel costs of $3.70–$3.75 per gallon and adjusted non-fuel unit cost growth of 3.5%–4.0%.

Southwest Airlines' third quarter adjusted EPS guidance of $0.50–$0.75 brackets the $0.57 consensus. However, management cut its full-year adjusted EPS outlook to $3.25–$4.25 from at least $4.00, making earnings delivery a key focus.

Seeking Alpha’s Quant system rates the stock 'hold' at 3.11, with A+ grades for valuation and growth, C+ grades for profitability and momentum, and D+ for revisions.

On the other hand, Seeking Alpha analyst Jaden Mealy maintains a Buy rating, citing Southwest’s commercial transformation and pricing gains, while flagging fuel and execution risks.

Investors will watch whether stronger revenue can offset fuel and operating costs and help stabilize earnings expectations.

data.title: Data centers may benefit from massive rural utility loan, US official says
data.description:
By Leah Douglas

A record-breaking $3.3 billion loan from the U.S. Department of Agriculture to a power plant in Georgia's Monroe County could potentially benefit data centers in the state, the agency's head of rural development said in an interview with Reuters.

The administration of President Donald Trump has supported the rapid expansion of data centers, despite their unpopularity with communities concerned about water use and utility costs. Democrats are attempting to capitalize on that discontent in November's midterm elections.

Glen Smith, the USDA's Under Secretary for Rural Development, said in the Thursday interview that he hopes to secure more funding for such projects.

Here are more details:

  • The USDA announced on Tuesday the loan to Oglethorpe Power Corporation, the largest ever given under the agency's Rural Utilities Service.

  • Smith said the plant will serve 38 rural utility cooperatives and support growing industry in the state, including potentially data centers.

  • Last year, Google purchased nearly 1,000 acres of land in Monroe County for a data center.

  • Oglethorpe spokesperson Blair Romero said in an email, "This facility is not dedicated to serving a data center. The new facility will help our Member cooperatives meet growing electricity demand across their communities."

  • Smith said he plans to meet with congressional appropriators next week and request more money for such loans. "We have almost $8.6 billion in requests, and we're only into our fiscal year one month," he said.

  • Smith said rural areas can benefit from data centers, "but you have to have the infrastructure in place. and that's where rural utilies and rural development comes into play."

  • Data centers are driving US electricity use to record highs and in some regions, demanding more power than grids can supply.

  • The Trump administration has not sought to regulate data center construction, instead asking tech companies to pledge not to pass on electricity costs to consumers.

data.title: Arista Networks CEO Is One of the World's Richest Women. She Just Sold $34M in Stock. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mackenzie Tatananni

Arista Networks CEO Jayshree Ullal, one of the wealthiest women in the world, cashed in millions worth of company stock during a run-up this month that pushed shares to record highs.

A filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission shows Ullal sold 158,543 Arista shares on Oct. 8 and Oct. 9, at prices ranging from $217 to $217.35, or $34.4 million in total.

The stock was held in three separate trusts, including two for Ullal's children. Following the sales, Ullal owns nearly 25 million shares indirectly and just 9,917 shares directly.

In all, the holdings represent 2% of Arista's 1.26 billion shares outstanding. Ullal's stake in the company was worth over $4.6 billion based on Thursday's closing price of $185.58.

The recent sales were conducted under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan Ullal adopted on Nov. 14, 2025. These arrangements are meant to shield company insiders from allegations of illegal trading.

The plan permits Ullal to sell up to 5,726,000 shares of common stock, as well as an unspecified number of shares earned in connection with grants of performance-restricted stock units, before it expires on Feb. 20, 2027.

Ullal's stake in Arista has made her one of the world's wealthiest women and a rare non-founder executive to reach that tier. The Bloomberg Billionaires Index pegs her net worth at around $7.76 billion, meaning more than half her fortune is tied to the cloud-networking company.

Arista shares have handily outpaced the broader market this year, surging 39% against a 13% gain for the benchmark S&P 500.

The stock jumped in early August after Arista reported better-than-expected earnings for the second quarter. Shares touched a record high of $217.41 and closed at a record $216.74 as recently as Oct. 9, though they have since pulled back from those levels.

Arista was named a Barron's stock pick in November 2025. Since that recommendation was made, shares have risen 35%.

Inside Scoop is a regular Barron's feature covering stock transactions by corporate executives and board members — so-called insiders — as well as large shareholders, politicians, and other prominent figures. Due to their insider status, these investors are required to disclose stock trades with the Securities and Exchange Commission or other regulatory groups.

THIS ANNOUNCEMENT CONTAINS INSIDE INFORMATION FOR THE PURPOSES OF ARTICLE 7 OF THE UK VERSION OF REGULATION (EU) NO. 596/2014, AS IT FORMS PART OF UK DOMESTIC LAW BY VIRTUE OF THE EUROPEAN UNION (WITHDRAWAL) ACT 2018, AS AMENDED.

​

16 October 2026

​

Roadside Real Estate plc

(“Roadside”, the “Company” or the “Group”)

Proposed Placing of Existing Ordinary Shares

and Intention to Deal

Roadside Real Estate plc (AIM: ROAD), the UK energy forecourt real estate business, announces that, in accordance with the orderly market arrangements entered into by Davina Dickson and James Dickson, as announced by the Company on 13 August 2026, the Company has been notified that Davina Dickson, James Dickson and certain other shareholders (together, the "Selling Shareholders") intend to sell up to an aggregate of 12,753,470 existing ordinary shares of £0.00860675675675676 each in the capital of the Company (the "Ordinary Shares")(the “Placing Shares”)  at a price of 51.0 pence per Ordinary Share (the "Placing Price"), by way of a placing to institutional investors (the "Placing").

The Placing Shares represent approximately 7.16 per cent. of the Company's issued share capital and have an aggregate value of approximately £6.5 million at the Placing Price.

The Placing will be effected by way of an accelerated bookbuild (the "Accelerated Bookbuild"), which will be launched immediately following publication of this announcement and will be available to eligible institutional investors.

Cavendish Capital Markets Limited ("Cavendish") and Shore Capital Stockbrokers Limited ("Shore Capital" and, together with Cavendish, the "Joint Bookrunners") are acting as Joint Bookrunners in connection with the Placing.

The Company will not receive any proceeds from the sale of the Placing Shares.

​

Intention to deal

The Company has also been notified that Tarncourt Capital Ltd ("Tarncourt"), an entity controlled by Charles Dickson, Chief Executive Officer of the Company, intends to acquire 5,500,000 Ordinary Shares from certain shareholders who are not members of the Concert Party (the "Tarncourt Purchase").

The Tarncourt Purchase is not part of the Placing and is intended to be completed prior to closure of the Accelerated Bookbuild.

Updates to Concert Party

The Company announced on 14 August 2026 that the shareholder concert party comprised Charles Dickson, Tarncourt, Davina Dickson, James Dickson and David Holdsworth (the “Concert Party”), following the removal of certain members, as agreed with the Panel on Takeovers and Mergers (the “Panel Executive”).

As at the date of this announcement, the Concert Party is interested in 95,550,354 Ordinary Shares, representing approximately 53.60 per cent. of the Company's issued share capital. Assuming completion of the Tarncourt Purchase, which would occur prior to the closure of the Accelerated Bookbuild, and the sale of shares proposed to be sold pursuant to the Placing, the Concert Party will hold in aggregate 89,196,884 Ordinary Shares, representing approximately 50.04 per cent. of the Company's issued share capital. Accordingly, the net effect of the proposed Tarncourt Purchase and the Placing would be to reduce the Concert Party's aggregate shareholding from approximately 53.60 per cent. to approximately 50.04 per cent of the Company's issued share capital. The Concert Party would therefore continue to hold shares carrying more than 50 per cent. of the voting rights of the Company.

Following the Tarncourt Purchase, and subsequently, the Placing, the Concert Party would continue to hold shares carrying more than 50 per cent. of the voting rights of the Company and, for so long as they continue to be acting in concert, no obligation to make an offer under Rule 9 of the City Code on Takeovers and Mergers will normally arise from acquisitions of interests in shares carrying voting rights by any member of the Concert Party.

Accelerated Bookbuild

The Placing will be effected by way of an Accelerated Bookbuild, which will be launched immediately following the release of this Announcement, and will be available to eligible institutional investors.

data.title: Weston, Baytex, Docebo at 52-Week Highs on News
data.description:
Baytex Energy Corp. (T.BTE) Hit a new 52-Week High of $7.51. This energy company has seen the Zacks Consensus Estimate for its current year earnings increasing 64% over the last 60 days.

Docebo Inc (T.DCBO) Hit a new 52-Week High of $39.86. Docebo announced today that it will hold a conference call to discuss its third quarter fiscal year 2026 results on Friday, November 6.

EverGen Infrastructure Corp. (V.EVGN) Hit a new 52-Week High of 80 cents. No news stories available today.

Gibson Energy Inc. (T.GEI) Hit a new 52-Week High of $33.48. Gibson announced today that it expects to release its 2026 third-quarter financial and operating results on Monday, November 2, 2026, after the close of North American markets.

High Arctic Energy Services Inc (T.HWO) Hit a new 52-Week High of $1.31. No news stories available.

InPlay Oil Corp. (T.IPO) Hit a new 52-Week High of $19.43. InPlay has declared a monthly cash dividend of $0.09 per common share payable on October 30, to shareholders of record at the close of business on October 15.

Loblaw Companies Ltd (T.L) Hit a new 52-Week High of $69.10. Loblaw has delivered a powerful run in recent years, and the question now is whether the cash flowing out of the business is enough to justify where the share price sits today.

Lake Victoria Gold Ltd. (V.LVG) Hit a new 52-Week High of 38.5 cents. The global gold market was valued at US$291.68 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach US$400 billion by the end of 2030, a compound annual growth rate of 6.51% over 2025 to 2030, according to Virtue Market Research.

Omni-Lite Industries Canada Inc. (V.OML) Hit a new 52-Week High of $3.20. Last month, Omni-Lite granted a total of 290,000 stock options and 60,000 restricted share units of the Company to certain directors and officers of the Company pursuant to its Long-Term Performance Incentive Plan.

Paramount Resources Ltd (T.POU) Hit a new 52-Week High of $34.17. Paramount declared a cash dividend of $0.05 per common share that will be payable on October 30, to shareholders of record on October 15.

Radius Gold Inc. (V.RDU) Hit a new 52-Week High of 28.5 cents. No news stories available today.

Suncor Energy Inc (T.SU) Hit a new 52-Week High of $108.82. No news stories available today.

Whitecap Resources Inc. (T.WCP) Hit a new 52-Week High of $20.02. Whitecap announces that it intends to release its third-quarter 2026 results after market close on Wednesday, October 28, and has scheduled a conference call and webcast to begin promptly at 9:00 am MT (11:00 am ET) on Thursday, October 29.

George Weston Limited (T.WN) Hit a new 52-Week High of $109.63. Weston recently announced a total dividend of $0.23 per share with the ex-dividend date set for 2026-09-15, including $0.23 per share cash dividend payable on 2026-10-01.
